title: Negotiating and persuading / Guteganya na kugumana
bridge: Mu gaciri, kuguma bantu tubyara gutumira amashusho agafite ubwoko nk’ ‘wibe we’ cyangwa ‘wabyitse’, n’ubushimi mu magambo yo hagati y’ ‘kugirango’. Mu Icyongereza, B2 ishatse icyo kiboneko gishigikira kandi gikwiye, kugira ‘would’, ‘could’, ‘might’ na ‘I was wondering if...’. Kwigomeka ku guhindura ‘gutanga ikibazo cy’ubwoko’ nk’ ‘to make a counteroffer’ (byihuse) ariko igisubizo ‘to suggest’ ntigishobora gutumwa mu bushimi mu Icyongereza, ahubwo igishobora gutumwa mu mbonera w’igisubizo (suggest + infinitive). Uretse ho, ‘tag questions’ kugirango ubone ibintu byagombye (isn't it?) ntibishobora kugirana ubwoko n’ ‘ese’, kubera mu Icyongereza bishobora kugana n’ubushakashatsi bw’igisubizo cy’umugambi w’umunsi.
rule: Kugirango witegeze no kuguma mu Icyongereza B2, tubyara: 1) Amasubirizo y’ubushakashatsi kugirango ubone ubwoko: 'would' (I would appreciate...), 'could' (Could we...), 'might' (That might work). 2) Amashusho y’ubwoko: 'I was wondering if...', 'Would it be possible to...?', 'If you could..., that would be...'. 3) Amasubirizo y’ubwoko kugirango ubone ubwoko: 'That's a fair point, but...', 'I see what you mean, however...'. 4) Amasubirizo y’ubwoko kugirango ubone ubwoko: 'What if we...?', 'How about...? + -ing', 'Would you be open to...?'. 5) Ubushimi bw’ibintu by’ubwoko: 'If we lowered the price, would you buy two?' (ubushimi bw’ibiri). Ku byerekeye kuguma, tubyara amasubirizo nk’ ‘Think of it this way...’, ‘The way I see it...’, ‘It's worth considering that...’. Byihuse: mu Icyongereza, ‘suggest’ na ‘recommend’ byagombwa kugirana n’ubushakashatsi n’ubwoko bw’igisubizo (nta ‘s’), cyangwa n’ubwoko bw’igisubizo: ‘I suggest that we wait’ / ‘I suggest waiting’. Ntushobora gutumira ubushimi nk’mu gaciri.

concept_examples.text: Could we possibly meet halfway on the price?
concept_examples.translation: Ese twishobora gusanganira mu kiremwa cy’ububiko?
concept_examples.phonetic: /kʊd wi ˈpɒsəbli miːt ˌhæfˈweɪ ɒn ðə praɪs/

concept_examples.text: I was wondering if you might consider a discount for bulk orders.
concept_examples.translation: Nari ntekereza no kubona ese mushobora kugaba ububiko mu bihe byinshi.
concept_examples.phonetic: /aɪ wɒz ˈwʌndərɪŋ ɪf ju maɪt kənˈsɪdər ə dɪskaʊnt fɔː bʌlk ˈɔːrdərz/

concept_examples.text: What if we extend the deadline by a week? That could work for both of us.
concept_examples.translation: N’ese tubyara kugabanya ubushakashatsi bw’igihe umunsi? Ibyo bishobora kuguma abakorera babiri.
concept_examples.phonetic: /wɒt ɪf wi ɪkˈstend ðə dedlaɪn baɪ ə wiːk ðæt kʊd wɜːrk fɔːr boʊθ əv ʌs/

concept_examples.text: If you agree to a lower price, we'll sign the contract today.
concept_examples.translation: N’ubwo mufite ububiko bw’ubwoko, turishobora kugenzura ubushakashatsi nuza.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ɪf ju əˈɡriː tʊ ə loʊər praɪs wiːl saɪn ðə ˈkɒntrækt təˈdeɪ/

common_error.wrong: I suggest that we should wait until next week.
common_error.correct: I suggest that we wait until next week.
common_error.correct_alt: I suggest waiting until next week.
common_error.explanation: Ibikorwa by’ubushakashatsi by’igisubizo ‘sugiero que debamos esperar’ n’ubushimi ‘should’. Mu Icyongereza, nyuma y’ ‘suggest’ (na ‘recommend’, ‘propose’), tubyara ubushimi bw’Icyongereza, ubwoko bw’igisubizo (nta ‘s’ na nta ‘should’). Mushobora gutumira ubwoko bw’igisubizo nk’ikiganiro. Byihuse ko ubushimi bw’igaciri ntibishobora gutumwa mu buryo bw’ubwoko; mu Icyongereza tubyara ubwoko bw’igisubizo kuri buri wese, byoroshye kuri ‘he/she/it’.

examples.original: Would it be possible to get an extension?
examples.phonetic: /wʊd ɪt bi ˈpɒsəbl tə ɡet ən ɪkˈstenʃən/
examples.translation: Ese byishobora kugabanywa ubushakashatsi bw’igihe?
examples.note: Tubyara ‘would’ ahandi ‘will’ kugirango ubone ubwoko, nk’ ‘Ese byishobora?’ mu gaciri.

examples.original: I was wondering if you could lower the price.
examples.phonetic: /aɪ wɒz ˈwʌndərɪŋ ɪf ju kʊd ˈloʊər ðə praɪs/
examples.translation: Nari ntekereza no kubona ese mushobora kugura ububiko.
examples.note: Ubwoko bw’ ‘I was wondering if...’ ni bw’ubwoko mu bihe byinshi. Ntushobora gutumira ‘I wondered’ kubera ko ni bw’ubwoko.

examples.original: Could we possibly agree on a different payment schedule?
examples.phonetic: /kʊd wi ˈpɒsəbli əˈɡriː ɒn ə ˈdɪfrənt ˈpeɪmənt ˈʃedjuːl/
examples.translation: Ese twishobora kugabanya ubushakashatsi bw’ubushakashatsi bw’igihe?
examples.note: ‘Possibly’ ni bw’ubwoko. Mu gaciri tubyara ‘¿Podríamos quizás?’, ariko ‘possibly’ bishobora kugana nyuma y’ubwoko.

examples.original: That's a fair point, but we can't go below ten percent.
examples.phonetic: /ðæts ə feər pɔɪnt bʌt wi kænt ɡəʊ bɪˈloʊ ten pəˈsent/
examples.translation: Ni ubwoko bw’ubwoko, ariko ntushobora kugura ubwoko bw’abiri.
examples.note: Guteganya ubwoko bw’umunyamuryango (‘That's a fair point’) ni cyo kintu cy’ubwoko mbere y’ubwoko.

examples.original: If you agree to a longer contract, we could offer a better rate.
examples.phonetic: /ɪf ju əˈɡriː tʊ ə ˈlɒŋɡər ˈkɒntrækt wi kʊd ˈɒfər ə ˈbetər reɪt/
examples.translation: N’ubwo mufite ubushakashatsi bw’ubushakashatsi, twishobora kugura ububiko bw’ubwoko.
examples.note: Ubushimi bw’ibiri (if + past, would/could) bishobora kugabanywa n’ubushakashatsi bw’ubwoko.

examples.original: How about reducing the quantity instead of the price?
examples.phonetic: /haʊ əˈbaʊt rɪˈdjuːsɪŋ ðə ˈkwɒntəti ɪnˈsted əv ðə praɪs/
examples.translation: Ese byishobora kugura ububiko bw’ubwoko ahandi bw’ububiko?
examples.note: ‘How about + -ing’ ni ubwoko bw’ubwoko bw’ubwoko.

examples.original: Think of it this way: a lower upfront cost saves you money in the long run.
examples.phonetic: /θɪŋk əv ɪt ðɪs weɪ ə loʊər ʌpˈfrʌnt kɒst seɪvz ju ˈmʌni ɪn ðə lɒŋ rʌn/
examples.translation: Tekereza bya ha: ububiko bw’ubushakashatsi bw’ubushakashatsi bukugura amafaranga mu bihe byinshi.
examples.note: Ubwoko bw’ ‘Think of it this way’ ni bw’ubwoko bw’ubwoko bw’ubwoko.

examples.original: Would you be open to a trial period for three months?
examples.phonetic: /wʊd ju bi ˈoʊpən tʊ ə ˈtraɪəl ˈpɪəriəd fɔː θriː mʌnθs/
examples.translation: Ese mufite ubushakashatsi bw’ubushakashatsi bw’amezi atatu?
examples.note: ‘Open to’ ni ubwoko bw’ubwoko ntibishobora kugirana ubwoko mu gaciri; bishobora kubwiye ‘dispuesto a considerar’.

examples.original: If we meet your deadline, will you extend the payment terms?
examples.phonetic: /ɪf wi miːt jɔːr dedlaɪn wɪl ju ɪkˈstend ðə ˈpeɪmənt tɜːmz/
examples.translation: N’ubwo tubyara kugabanya ubushakashatsi bw’ubushakashatsi, ese mushobora kugabanya ubushakashatsi bw’ubushakashatsi?
examples.note: Ubushimi bw’ubushakashatsi (if + present, will) bishobora kugabanywa n’ubushakashatsi bw’ubwoko na kugura ubushakashatsi bw’ubwoko.

examples.original: I'm confident we can find a solution that works for both sides.
examples.phonetic: /aɪm ˈkɒnfɪdənt wi kæn faɪnd ə səˈluːʃən ðæt wɜːks fɔːr boʊθ saɪdz/
examples.translation: Ntekereza ko twishobora kugura ubushakashatsi bukwiye kuri buri wese.
examples.note: Gutumira ‘I'm confident’ ahandi ‘I think’ bishobora kuguma na kuguma.

title: Giving and justifying opinions in depth / Gutanga no kugereka ibitekerezo mu mubare
bridge: Mu ikinyarwanda, ni byaba birenze gutanga ibitekerezo bigaragara nk’uko biteye kandi bikoresha amagambo nk’ ‘ntekereza ko’ cyangwa ‘ntekereza ko’. Mu igishushimane, kugereka ibitekerezo mu mubare birashoboka kubyara amagambo nk’ ‘the reason being’, ‘due to’, ‘given that’, na kubyara amahomere nk’ ‘if... then...’. Nta wigeze kugira ubwoba kuri ‘según mi opinión’ (igishushimane: ‘according to my opinion’ - si kigoye, bikwiye ‘in my opinion’). Mu igishushimane, amagambo nk’ ‘would’, ‘could’ ari byatanze kugira ngo ubufasha ubitekerezo no kugeresha ibintu.
rule: Kugira ngo utange no ugereke ibitekerezo mu mubare mu igishushimane, koresha: 1) Amagambo y’ibitekerezo: ‘In my view’, ‘From my perspective’, ‘I would argue that’, ‘It seems to me that’. 2) Kugereka: ‘The reason for this is’, ‘This is due to’, ‘Given that’, ‘Considering that’. 3) Gutegura: ‘However’, ‘On the other hand’, ‘While it is true that...’, ‘Nevertheless’. 4) Amahomere yo kwerekana: ‘If... then’, ‘Unless...’, ‘Provided that...’. 5) Amahomere y’inguvu-ikorwa: ‘This leads to’, ‘As a result’, ‘Consequently’. Mu mubare w’ibyo B2: Ibyo bikwiye ni ukuntanga amagambo menshi no kwigisha ibintu mu buryo bw’umwimerere. Kanga ubwoko bw’amagambo y’ubwoko no gutanga igihe cy’amagambo (present perfect vs. past simple) ubwo utanga ibiranga.

concept_examples.text: In my view, remote work has increased productivity, the reason being that employees avoid long commutes.
concept_examples.translation: Ntekereza ko ubukorikori bw’ibiro byatanze ubushobozi bw’ubukorikori, inguvu ni ukubera ko abakorikira batabura amabara menshi.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ɪn maɪ vjuː, rɪˈmoʊt wɜːrk hæz ˈɪnkriːst ˌprɒdʌkˈtɪvəti, ðə ˈriːzn ˈbiːɪŋ ðæt ˌemploʊˈiːz əˈvɔɪd lɔːŋ kəˈmjuːts/

concept_examples.text: I would argue that investing in education yields long-term benefits, given that it improves social mobility.
concept_examples.translation: Nzagira ko gutanga amafranga mu kwifozwa kirimo amaherezo mu gihe cyateye, kubera ko bikoresha ubwingeranire mu bwami.
concept_examples.phonetic: /aɪ wʊd ˈɑːrgjuː ðæt ɪnˈvestɪŋ ɪn ˌedʒuˈkeɪʃn jiːldz lɔːŋ tɜːrm ˈbenɪfɪts, ˈɡɪvn ðæt ɪt ɪmˈpruːvz ˈsoʊʃl moʊˈbɪləti/

concept_examples.text: From my perspective, the new policy is flawed, due to the fact that it ignores regional differences.
concept_examples.translation: Mu buryo bwangu, itegeko rishya rifite ibibazo, kubera ko ntabwo ifite ubwoko bw’ibintu by’igihugu.
concept_examples.phonetic: /frɒm maɪ pərˈspektɪv, ðə nuː ˈpɒləsi ɪz flɔːd, djuː tuː ðə fækt ðæt ɪt ɪɡˈnɔːrz ˈriːdʒənl ˈdɪfrənsɪz/

concept_examples.text: It seems to me that we should prioritize renewable energy, otherwise we will face severe climate consequences.
concept_examples.translation: Ntekereza ko dufite gutanga ubushakashatsi ku mafura yifashishijwe, kugira ngo nituburire ibyago by’ibindi by’igihugu.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ɪt siːmz tuː miː ðæt wiː ʃʊd praɪˈɒrɪtaɪz rɪˈnjuːəbl ˈenərdʒi, ˈʌðəwaɪz wiː wɪl feɪs sɪˈvɪər ˈklaɪmət ˈkɒnsɪkwənsɪz/

common_error.wrong: According to my opinion, the government should do more for education.
common_error.correct: In my opinion, the government should do more for education.
common_error.correct_alt: From my point of view, the government should do more for education.
common_error.explanation: Mu ikinyarwanda tugira ‘según mi opinión’ (igishushimane: ‘according to my opinion’), ariko mu igishushimane nta magambo nk’ibyo; ‘according to’ bikoreshwa na buri kintu (according to the report). Ibyo bikwiye ni ‘in my opinion’ cyangwa ‘from my point of view’. Ibi byago birenze kuri abanyarwanda kubera ko ‘según’ mu igishushimane bikoreshwa nk’ ‘according to’.

examples.original: In my view, the film was overrated.
examples.phonetic: /ɪn maɪ vjuː, ðə fɪlm wɒz ˌoʊvərˈreɪtɪd/
examples.translation: Ntekereza ko ifilimu yarimo ubushakashatsi.

examples.original: I strongly believe that recycling should be mandatory.
examples.phonetic: /aɪ ˈstrɔːŋli bɪˈliːv ðæt rɪˈsaɪklɪŋ ʃʊd biː ˈmændətɔːri/
examples.translation: Ntekereza neza ko gutunganya ibintu bikwiye.
examples.note: ‘Strongly believe’ bikoresha ubushakashatsi; mu ikinyarwanda tugira ‘ntekereza neza’.

examples.original: As far as I'm concerned, the project is on track.
examples.phonetic: /æz fɑːr æz aɪm kənˈsɜːrnd, ðə ˈprɒdʒekt ɪz ɒn træk/
examples.translation: Mu buryo bwangu, igikorwa kirimo ubwoko.
examples.note: Iyi mugo yifusha kugira ngo utange ubitekerezo bwawe.

examples.original: The reason being that prices have risen significantly.
examples.phonetic: /ðə ˈriːzn ˈbiːɪŋ ðæt ˈpraɪsɪz hæv ˈrɪzən sɪɡˈnɪfɪkəntli/
examples.translation: Inguvu ni ukubera ko amafaranga yatanze neza.
examples.note: Ibyo bikoreshwa nyuma y’ubwoko kugira ngo ubyare ibyago by’ibyishushanyije.

examples.original: Due to the lack of funding, the program was cancelled.
examples.phonetic: /djuː tuː ðə læk ɒv ˈfʌndɪŋ, ðə ˈproʊɡræm wɒz ˈkænsəld/
examples.translation: Kubera ko ntabwo amafranga, igikorwa cyagenze.
examples.note: ‘Due to’ ni byaba birenze kurushaho ‘because of’. Kanga ‘to’ no kugira ubwoba kuri ‘because’.

examples.original: Given that the economy is unstable, we should be cautious.
examples.phonetic: /ˈɡɪvn ðæt ði ɪˈkɒnəmi ɪz ʌnˈsteɪbl, wiː ʃʊd biː ˈkɔːʃəs/
examples.translation: Kubera ko ubukorikori bufite ubwoko, dufite kuba na ubwoba.
examples.note: ‘Given that’ ni byaba birenze kugira ngo ubyare ubwoko cyangwa ibintu by’ubushakashatsi.

examples.original: While it is true that technology has drawbacks, it also opens up new possibilities.
examples.phonetic: /waɪl ɪt ɪz truː ðæt tekˈnɒlədʒi hæz ˈdrɔːbæks, ɪt ˈɔːlsoʊ ˈoʊpənz ʌp nuː ˌpɒsəˈbɪlətiz/
examples.translation: Nuko byaba byari byo, ubushakashatsi bw’ubushakashatsi bworoshye, ariko bukoresha amaherezo menshi.
examples.note: Iyi mugo yifusha kugira ngo ubyare ubwoko bw’ibintu bibiri.

examples.original: Unless we address climate change now, future generations will suffer.
examples.phonetic: /ənˈles wiː əˈdres ˈklaɪmət tʃeɪndʒ naʊ, ˈfjuːtʃər ˌdʒenəˈreɪʃnz wɪl ˈsʌfər/
examples.translation: Kugira ngo nituburire ibyago by’ibindi by’igihugu, dufite gutanga ubushakashatsi ku mafura yifashishijwe.
examples.note: Koresha ‘unless’ nk’ ‘kugira ngo’ (amahomere y’ubwoba).

examples.original: If the government invested more in healthcare, the overall well-being would improve.
examples.phonetic: /ɪf ðə ˈɡʌvənmənt ɪnˈvestɪd mɔːr ɪn ˈhelθkeər, ði ˌoʊvərˈɔːl ˌwelˈbiːɪŋ wʊd ɪmˈpruːv/
examples.translation: Iyo serikwete yatanze amafranga mu buzima, ubuzima bw’ubwoko bwose bukorera neza.
examples.note: Ikindi kintu cy’ubwoba kugira ngo ubyare ubwoko. Mu igishushimane, tugira igihe cy’amagambo (past simple) mu mugo y’ ‘if’.

title: Hypothesising about the past / Gutegura ibyagenze
bridge: Mu gaciro, kugutegura ibyagenze tubika 'habría + participio' cyangwa 'hubiera + participio', ariko mu gaciro cyongereza kuri kinyabiziga: 'would have + past participle' kugira ngo ubone ububiko n'ubundi 'had + past participle' kugira ngo ubone ububiko (third conditional). Ikibazo kinini ni guhindura 'si habría' kuri 'if would have', ariko mu gaciro cyongereza ububiko ntibikubaho 'would'. Nanone, mu gaciro cyongereza harimo 'might have' na 'could have' kugira ngo ubone ububiko cyangwa ubushobozi, mu gaciro kinyarwanda bikorwa n'ubushobozi 'podría haber' cyangwa 'quizás habría'.
rule: Kugutegura ibyagenze mu gaciro cyongereza, tubika 'third conditional' n'ibindi bikorwa n'ubushobozi. Ikinyabiziga ni: 'If + past perfect (had + participle), would have + past participle'. Inyu: 'If I had studied, I would have passed'. Nanone tubika bikorwa n'ubushobozi: 'could have' (ubushobozi cyangwa ububiko), 'might have' (ububiko), 'should have' (icyerekezo cyangwa ikibazo). Mu gucumbagiza cyangwa mu gutumye, tubika 'wish + past perfect' (ojalá hubiera). Ntibikubaho 'would have' mu 'if'. Mu ibibazo, ububiko n'ubundi: 'Would you have...?'

concept_examples.text: If I had known, I would have told you.
concept_examples.translation: Niyo nari menye, nari ngutegereje.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ɪf aɪ hæd noʊn, aɪ wʊd hæv toʊld juː/

concept_examples.text: She might have missed the train.
concept_examples.translation: Yemwe yari asubiye atambukira.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ʃiː maɪt hæv mɪst ðə treɪn/

concept_examples.text: We could have won the match.
concept_examples.translation: Turi twari dufite ubushakashatsi.
concept_examples.phonetic: /wiː kʊd hæv wʌn ðə mætʃ/

concept_examples.text: I wish I had studied more.
concept_examples.translation: Nuba hari nari somye neza.
concept_examples.phonetic: /aɪ wɪʃ aɪ hæd ˈstʌdɪd mɔːr/

common_error.wrong: If I would have known, I would have told you.
common_error.correct: If I had known, I would have told you.
common_error.correct_alt: Had I known, I would have told you.
common_error.explanation: Ikibazo kiki kigenzwa kubera mu gaciro kinyarwanda tubika 'Si hubiera sabido' n'abanyeshuri bamwe bahindura 'hubiera' kuri 'would have', ariko mu gaciro cyongereza ububiko 'if' ntibikubaho 'would'. Ibyo bikubiyemo ni 'had + participio' mu gucumbagiza. Kugira ngo ubure, remera 'would' bikubaho mu gucumbagiza kuri ububiko.

examples.original: If she had left earlier, she wouldn't have missed the flight.
examples.phonetic: /ɪf ʃiː hæd lɛft ˈɜːrliər, ʃiː ˈwʊdnt hæv mɪst ðə flaɪt/
examples.translation: Niyo yari yatanze, atari kwishyira hejuru.
examples.note: Ikinyabiziga: 'If + past perfect, would not have + participio'.

examples.original: They would have arrived on time if the traffic hadn't been so bad.
examples.phonetic: /ðeɪ wʊd hæv əˈraɪvd ɒn taɪm ɪf ðə ˈtræfɪk ˈhædnt biːn soʊ bæd/
examples.translation: Bari bashoboye gutura mu gihe niba ubushorishori ntibwari bishize.
examples.note: Ububiko 'if' bishobora kuba ahantu hasi nta koma.

examples.original: You should have called me.
examples.phonetic: /juː ʃʊd hæv kɔːld miː/
examples.translation: Wari wabaye wanjye.
examples.note: Kugira 'should have' kugira ngo ubone ikibazo cyangwa gutumye.

examples.original: He could have been a doctor.
examples.phonetic: /hiː kʊd hæv biːn ə ˈdɒktər/
examples.translation: Yemwe yari ashoboye kuba udoktori.
examples.note: Gutumye ubushobozi cyangwa ububiko ntibwigenze.

examples.original: They might have forgotten the meeting.
examples.phonetic: /ðeɪ maɪt hæv fərˈɡɒtn ðə ˈmiːtɪŋ/
examples.translation: Bari bashoboye kwishyura ubutaka.
examples.note: Gutumye ububiko ntibwizi mu byagenze.

examples.original: I wish I had accepted the job offer.
examples.phonetic: /aɪ wɪʃ aɪ hæd əkˈsɛptɪd ðə dʒɒb ˈɒfər/
examples.translation: Nuba hari nari ngabanye igishushanyo cy'ubutegetsi.
examples.note: Tubika 'wish + past perfect' kugira ngo ubone ikibazo.

examples.original: If only we had listened to the weather forecast.
examples.phonetic: /ɪf ˈoʊnli wiː hæd ˈlɪsənd tuː ðə ˈwɛðər ˈfɔːrkæst/
examples.translation: Nuba hari twari tumvise ubushakashatsi bw'ijoro.
examples.note: 'If only' ni ikinyabiziga kizana kuri ububiko ntibwizi.

title: Discussing abstract concepts / Kuganira ibyago by’umwuka
bridge: Mu gaciri, kugana ibyago by’umwuka, dushtura gushtuka mu gutumira umushushanyo (‘ni byinshi ko...’, ‘ntekereza ko...’) n’amatsinda yishushanyo. Mu Icyongereza, gutumira umushushanyo biranguruka kuri verb nk’ ‘suggest’, ‘recommend’, ‘demand’, n’ibiganiro nk’ ‘it is essential that...’. Nanone, mu Icyongereza, amazina y’ibyago by’umwuka nk’ ‘freedom’ cyangwa ‘justice’ birahishurwa bigenewe akagari kuki bikorwa ibyago by’umwuka, kandi mu gaciri byahishuwe na ‘la’ (‘la libertad’). Kugeza ahantu, mu Icyongereza, bashimishwa ‘do’ kugaba n’kugombera, n’amajambo ntibikurikira umuntu.
rule: Kugana ibyago by’umwuka mu Icyongereza ku murongo B2, wabimenya: 1. Amazina y’ibyago by’umwuka mu singuli/mu bishishito bigenewe akagari kugana ibyago by’umwuka (‘Freedom is important’ vs ‘La libertad es importante’). 2. Imvugo yongereye na ‘that’ + umuhamya mu ndango y’umushushanyo nyuma y’imvugo y’igishushanyo cyangwa y’igikorwa (‘I suggest that she be...’) n’na hamwe n’amajambo (‘It is crucial that he attend’). 3. Amatsinda y’kuvuga ibitekerezo: ‘In my opinion’, ‘I believe that’, ‘It seems to me that’, utumira umushushanyo (nta nk’mu gaciri). 4. Gutumira imvugo y’ ‘which’ na ‘that’ kugena n’kugenura. 5. Imvugo y’ububiko kumenya ubwoko: ‘might’, ‘could’, ‘would’, ‘should’ kumenya ubwoko, ububiko cyangwa igishushanyo. 6. Ibiganiro by’umuntu (‘It is obvious that’, ‘It is worth considering’). Niba wibuka ko mu Icyongereza nta gukomoka kabiri, n’uko imvugo irimo Umuntu + Umuhamya + Ikintu.

title: Expressing complex emotions / Kugena ubwoba n’ibindi bwemotioni bikomeye
bridge: Mu gihugu cy’Espanya, hagati ya mbere tubona gutumira amagambo nk’ ‘estar’ hamwe n’igitabo cy’amagambo cyangwa ‘sentirse’ kugena ubwoba, ariko mu gihugu cy’Angilitere bashimishije gusaba amagambo menshi, nk’amagambo y’ubwoko bw’ibiri, amagambo y’ubwoko bw’ibiri hamwe n’ijambo ry’ubwoko bw’ibiri, n’ururimi rw’ubwoba. Ikibazo kinini ni guhindura ‘tengo miedo de’ kuri ‘I have fear of’ aho kuri ‘I'm afraid of’. Nanone, ururimi rw’Angilitere rugahinda ibintu bikomeye ururimi rw’Espanya ntirubigisha n’amagambo menshi, nk’ ‘frustrated’ (frustrado) vs. ‘annoyed’ (molesto), cyangwa ‘overwhelmed’ (abrumado) idontaho igice kinini. Reba neza ku magambo y’ubwoko bw’ibiri n’amagambo y’ubwoko bw’ibiri yongereye igitabo cy’amagambo.
rule: Kugena ubwoba n’ibindi bwemotioni bikomeye mu gihugu cy’Angilitere, bashimishije: 1) Amagambo y’ubwoko bw’ibiri hamwe n’ijambo ry’ubwoko bw’ibiri: ‘angry about/at’, ‘frustrated with’, ‘disappointed in/with’, ‘excited about’, ‘worried about’, ‘ashamed of’, ‘proud of’. 2) Amagambo y’ubwoko bw’ibiri hamwe n’ijambo ry’ubwoko bw’ibiri cyangwa ‘feel like’ + gerundio kugena ubwoba bw’akanya. 3) Amagambo nk’ ‘get’ + igitabo cy’amagambo kugena ubwoba bw’ubwoba bw’akanya (get frustrated, get overwhelmed). 4) Amagambo y’ubwoko bw’ibiri hamwe n’ijambo ry’ubwoko bw’ibiri kugena ubwoba bikomeye: ‘homesick’, ‘heartbroken’, ‘overwhelmed’. 5) Amagambo y’ubwoko bw’ibiri kugena ubwoba bukomeye: ‘on cloud nine’ (muy feliz), ‘down in the dumps’ (deprimido). Reba neza ‘nervous’ bushobora gutumwa kugena ubwoba bw’akanya, ‘anxious’ bushobora gutumwa kugena ubwoba bukomeye; ‘upset’ ni bukomeye kurusha ‘sad’. Ntushimire ‘I have’ hamwe n’ubwoba mu gihugu cy’Angilitere, usibye mu magambo nk’ ‘I have a feeling’.

title: Formal Writing: Reports and Emails / Ukuandika bihuze: ibiro n’email
bridge: Mu igifaransa, ukuandika bihuze bishobora kuba bigeze kandi bikoresha amatsinda menshi n’ibishushanyijwe. Mu Icyongereza, ubuhuze buzakurwa no kuba wigeze no kwangukana. Ikibazo k’ingirakamaro ni guhindura hasi ‘Le adjunto’ kuba ‘I attach’ (si ko) ahandi ‘Please find attached’ cyangwa ‘I have attached’. Nanone, mu Icyongereza bihuze, amatsinda nk’ ‘would’ na ‘could’ ari ngombwa kugira ubwubahwane, mu gihe mu igifaransa bikoresha ‘Podría’. Ikindi kibi k’ubwoko: mu Icyongereza ntibikoresha ‘usted’ cyangwa uburyo bwo kushushanya bwo kwubahwana, ariko bikoresha ubushobozi bw’ijambo n’amatsinda y’ubwubahwane.
rule: Kugira ngo uandike ibiro n’email bihuze mu Icyongereza ku murongo wa B2, ni ngombwa kugira ubwubahwane bwa kuri kandi ukoresheje: 1) Amatsinda y’ubwubahwane mu kubura na mu gutura: ‘Dear Mr. Smith’, ‘Dear Madam’, ‘Yours sincerely’, ‘Yours faithfully’. 2) Amatsinda n’ibyo bikorwa bihuze: ‘state’ (ahandi ‘say’), ‘require’ (ahandi ‘need’), ‘I would like to’ (ahandi ‘I want’), ‘I am writing to inform you’. 3) Uburyo bwo kushushanya bw’amatsinda: umutsinda w’iburyo, umubare w’ibyo bikorwa n’ibyo bikorwa, kandi ububiko bw’ibyo bikorwa cyangwa ububiko bw’ibyo bikorwa. 4) Kwigomeka guhitamo: andika ‘do not’ ahandi ‘don’t’, ‘I would’ ahandi ‘I’d’. 5) Kuri ibiro: koresha amatsinda y’ubwubahwane nk’ ‘Introduction’, ‘Findings’, ‘Recommendations’, na ubushobozi bw’ijambo bw’ubwubahwane nk’ ‘It was found that...’ (Byabonetse ko...). 6) Amatsinda y’ubwubahwane kugira ubwubahwane: ‘Could you please...’, ‘I would appreciate...’, ‘Would it be possible to...?’. Niba ubishaka kugira ubwubahwane mu Icyongereza, ntukoreshe ‘please’ mu mwisho w’ijambo (ni ko bihuze), ahubwo ukoreshe mu buryo cyangwa mbere y’umwanya.

title: Dealing with Conflict / Kugirira ibiribwa n’amahenyi
bridge: Mu gaciri, dusaba gusaba hasi (‘Nibagize utubwire’) cyangwa kugira ibyago by’amagambo ‘wowe ushoba’ kugirira ibiribwa. Mu Icyongereza, kwizera no kugirira ubwoba ni by’ingenzi: bashimishwa amagambo nk’ ‘could’ na ‘might’, n’ibiganiro nk’ ‘I feel...’ ahandi hose kugira ibyago by’amahoro. Ikibazo kinini ni guhindura ‘wowe ushoba’ kuba ‘you must’, kigira igice kinini; mu cyo kirenge, bashimishwa ‘you might want to’ cyangwe ‘maybe you could’.
rule: Kugirira ibiribwa mu Icyongereza ku murongo B2, bashimishwa imbarure z’ubwoba n’ururimi rw’ibanga. Ibintu by’ingenzi ni: 1) Amagambo y’ubwoba kugira ibyago by’ubwoba: ‘could’, ‘might’, ‘would’ (e.g. ‘We could try...’). 2) Ibiganiro by’ubwenge bwawe n’ubwenge bwawe ‘I feel’, ‘I think’, ‘I believe’ kugirira ibyago by’amahoro. 3) Imbarure z’ubwenge kugirira ibyago by’ubwoba: ‘If you..., we could...’. 4) Ibiganiro by’ubwoba: ‘I understand’, ‘I see your point’. 5) Ibibazo by’ibanga: ‘I wonder if you could...’. 6) Kugira ‘sorry’ kugirira ibyago by’ubwoba: ‘I'm sorry if that came across the wrong way’. Nta na kimwe kuri ‘you’ (e.g. ‘You are wrong’) kuba kigira igice kinini. Mu cyo kirenge, bashimishwa ‘I'm not sure that's accurate’ cyangwe ‘I see it differently’.

title: Summarising and Paraphrasing / Gutangaza no Kugiranganisha
bridge: Mu igifaransa, dute urupapuro rw'amagambo nk' 'o sea', 'es decir' na 'en resumen', ariko mu ngereza, amagambo yo kuganira yatanzwe neza kuri burundo canke mu giteganyi cy'umugambi, hamwe n'ibinyabiziga. Kwigomeka: mu ngereza, 'in summary' atari byinshi nk' 'in short' canke 'to sum up', na 'summarize' itangwa igice cyambere kirimo inyubakwa. Ubundi binyabiziga ni uko mu igifaransa dushaka kugaragaza umuntu, ariko mu ngereza, gutumiza amagambo no kugiranganisha birimo ubwokozi, ariko ntushobora kugaragaza umuntu mu magambo yose.
rule: Kugiranganisha no gutangaza mu ngereza ku murongo wa B2, tusiga amagambo nk' 'summarize', 'paraphrase', 'outline', 'restate', na ibinyabiziga nk' 'in other words', 'that is', 'to put it briefly', 'in a nutshell', 'to sum up', 'in short', 'all in all' na 'to recap'. Uburengo bw'ibintu ni: [Ibinyabiziga] + [igitangaza cy'ubwokozi]. Mu gutumiza amagambo, ubugambi bw'imigambi byihutirwa (nk' urupapuro rw'ubwokozi ku bwokozi, canke igitangaza cy'ubwokozi ku rwokozi) ariko ubwokozi bubonanye. Ibirebana: 'The study reveals a significant increase...' → 'In other words, the numbers went up a lot.' Kugiranganisha igitabo, ushobora kugena na 'The text is about...' canke 'The author argues that...'. Ushobora kugarura gutumiza 'en resumen' nk' 'in summary' mu buryo bwo kwigisha; onga 'in short' canke 'to sum up'. Nanone wigomeke ku buryo bwo kwitumiza 'actually' (ibigisha 'mu byarugero', si 'mu gihe kihitiye'), ariko mu gutangaza, 'in fact' canke 'actually' bitumizwa neza.

title: Using Idioms Naturally / Kubyara amashusho y’ikinyarwanda y’ingenzi
bridge: Mu gihugu, amashusho y’ikinyarwanda y’ingenzi yoroshye kenshi kandi yashyirwa mo mukuri n’amatsinda nk’ ‘gutwara’ cyangwa ‘kuba’ (ntese, ‘kuba nk’inka’). Mu Icyongereza, amashusho menshi y’ikinyarwanda y’ingenzi yashyirwa mo mukuri n’amatsinda y’igikorwa n’amazu y’ikinyarwanda, kandi yoroshye kenshi kandi yijanye n’ibintu. Ikibazo k’ingenzi ni guhindura amashusho y’ikinyarwanda y’ingenzi mu Icyongereza (ntese, ‘gutwara isura nziza’ ahubwo ‘kuba mu munezero’). Uretse, Icyongereza bishyura kuruta ‘to be’ mu gutanga nk’ ‘be over the moon’, mu gihugu bashyira ‘estar’ cyangwa ‘tener’. Reba ku kwigwa: amashusho y’ikinyarwanda y’ingenzi yamara y’ingenzi (‘kick the bucket’) n’icyandi (‘pass away’).
rule:
Kugirango wibyaye amashusho y’ikinyarwanda y’ingenzi mu Icyongereza, shirikiza ibyo ubifuzwa:
1. Soma amashusho y’ikinyarwanda y’ingenzi nk’ibintu by’ishusho, ntiby’ijambo.
2. Menya ubushakashatsi: bwite, butegetsi, butegetsi, cyangwa butegetsi. Ntese, ‘to be over the moon’ ni butegetsi, ariko ‘to be delighted’ ni bwite kurushaho.
3. Amashusho menshi y’ikinyarwanda y’ingenzi afite ubushakashatsi bw’ishusho atari ubw’ijambo. Ntese, ‘break the ice’ atavuga gutanga icyo kibazo, ariko gutanga icyo kibazo mu muryango w’ibintu.
4. Ni byoroshye mu kwivuga k’umunsi, ariko mu andishi y’ishengerege cyangwa y’ubucuruzi byashyirwa mo mukuri n’ubushakashatsi.
5. Amashusho y’ikinyarwanda y’ingenzi yamara y’ubushakashatsi bw’ipayi (ntese, ‘to be in hot water’ mu Icyongereza y’Amerika vs. ‘to be in a pickle’ mu buri se).
6. Ubushakashatsi n’uburyo bwo kwivuga ni by’ingenzi: amashusho y’ikinyarwanda y’ingenzi yoroshye kenshi kandi yijanye n’ibintu, n’amatsinda y’ubushakashatsi ni by’ingenzi mu muryango w’ibintu (ntese, ‘it’s raining cats and dogs’).
7. Ntamashusho y’ikinyarwanda y’ingenzi yose ni y’amatsinda; yamara ni iby’ijambo cyangwa iby’amazu (ntese, ‘a piece of cake’ = ibintu by’ingenzi).
8. Soma amatsinda y’ubushakashatsi: amashusho menshi y’ikinyarwanda y’ingenzi yashyirwa mo mukuri n’ubushakashatsi bw’ishusho (ntese, ‘he bit the bullet’), bityo shirikiza gutumika mu matsinda y’ubushakashatsi.

title: Academic and Professional Register / Ibirimo by’ishushanyo n’iby’akazi
bridge: Mu gihugu cy’English, mu by’ishushanyo n’iby’akazi, ubwokozi n’ubwoba bwakira n’uburyo bw’imiryango ifite ubwokozi, amagambo yo kwemeza n’uburyo bw’gutumiza amagambo, kandi mu ikinyarwanda tugomba gutumiza amagambo y’ubwokozi n’ubwoba nka ‘se’ cyangwa ‘uno’. Ikibazo cy’urupfu ni ukuguta ubwokozi bw’ubwoba (‘It is said that...’ → ‘Se dice que...’) ntiwibuka ko igihugu cy’English kiragomba umuntu w’ubwokozi cyangwa ubwokozi bw’ubwoba. Nanone, kugamburira ‘would’, ‘could’ n’ ‘might’ kugira ngo ubwokozi bw’ubwoba, mu ikinyarwanda tugomba gutumiza ubwokozi bw’ubwoba (‘podría ser’) ariko mu gihugu cy’English kiragomba ubwokozi bw’ubwoba n’ubwokozi bw’ubwoba. Nta gushaka kw’ubwokozi: ‘can’ na ‘will’ birimo, ariko mu by’ubwokozi n’ubwoba, ‘may’ na ‘would’ ni byo bitandukanye.
rule: Mu gihugu cy’English, mu by’ubwokozi n’ubwoba, ubwokozi bw’ubwoba (‘It was decided...’) ni ubwokozi bw’ubwoba (‘We decided...’) kugira ngo ubwokozi bw’ubwoba. Amagambo yo kwemeza (‘may’, ‘might’, ‘could’) ashobora kugamburira ubwokozi bw’ubwoba, na ‘would’ kugira ngo ubwokozi bw’ubwoba. Ubwokozi bw’ubwoba (gutumiza amagambo y’ubwokozi, e.g., ‘to decide’ → ‘decision’) ni byinshi mu gihugu cy’ishushanyo. Mu buryo bw’ubushakashatsi, amagambo yo kwemeza (don't → do not), na gutumiza amagambo yo kwemeza nka ‘however’, ‘furthermore’, ‘nevertheless’. Mu ikinyarwanda, ubwokozi bw’ubwoba ni ubwokozi bw’ubwoba n’uburyo bw’gutumiza ‘se’, n’ubwokozi bw’ubwoba (‘sería’, ‘podría’) kugira ngo ubwokozi bw’ubwoba. Wibuke ko igihugu cy’English nta mugenzi w’ubwokozi/ubwokozi, ariko kiragomba umuntu w’ubwokozi (usibye mu by’ubwokozi) n’uburyo bw’ubushakashatsi ni bw’ubwokozi. Kugira ubwokozi B2, wigenzere ubwokozi bw’ubwoba n’ubwokozi bw’ubwoba, amagambo yo kwemeza mu bwokozi n’ubwokozi (‘could have done’), n’ubwokozi bw’ ‘would’ mu by’ubwokozi bw’ubwoba.

common_error.correct: It is said that the problem is easy to solve.

common_error.explanation: Ikibazo cy’urupfu ni ukuguta ‘Se dice que...’ nka ‘It says that...’ cyangwa ‘Se says that...’ ahandi gutumiza ubwokozi bw’ubwoba ‘It is said that...’. Mu ikinyarwanda, ubwokozi bw’ubwoba n’ ‘se’ ni byinshi kugira ngo ubwokozi bw’ubwoba, ariko mu gihugu cy’English nta mugenzi w’ubwokozi; tugomba gutumiza ‘It + ubwokozi bw’ubwoba’ cyangwa ‘People/They’ nka umuntu w’ubwokozi. Nta ‘Se says’ (gutumiza ikinyarwanda) kandi nibuke ko ubwokozi bw’ubwoba biragomba ubwokozi ‘to be’ + ubwokozi bw’ubwoba, n’ubwokozi ‘It’ nka umuntu w’ubwokozi.
